note: Hand-built personal index page. Dense link lists, a fixed footer bar, decorative watermarks behind headings, no design system. Catches rules that assume a component-framework page. Owned by this project's author, so not redacted.
APP. A real product dashboard, open without login: ~880 visible elements, ~180 controls, ~80 icon-sized targets. The densest application chrome in the corpus.
APP. A drawing tool: ~90 icon-sized controls in toolbars and palettes, plus 19 form controls. The best evidence in the corpus for optical centring, icon-size consistency and small touch targets.

APP, and the false-positive detector. Built on a deliberate design system by people who know what they are doing, so findings here are suspect by default. Declares dark styles, which most app candidates do not.
APP. A data-table screen on the same design system as shadcn-dashboard. Two pages sharing one system is the sharpest test of the consistency family: it should stay silent across both.

APP. A social timeline on a different stack: columns, cards, avatars, inline media. Real content of varying length rather than lorem ipsum. Pixels kept, so the rules that read the render have evidence here.
APP. A map application with a search sidebar. The most form-dense page in the corpus at 25 controls, which is where label-proximity and control-border-contrast get their evidence.

APP, deliberately tiny. The canonical small application: one form, one list, filter states. A page this small should produce almost nothing, so anything it does produce is worth reading. Pixels kept, so the rules that read the render have evidence here.
Long-form editorial with a sticky header and real dark styles. Carries most of the corpus's evidence for the typography rules, which app screens barely exercise.
CJK script. The measure rule counts characters per line, an assumption that does not survive contact with Japanese: the comfortable measure is roughly half the Latin figure.
Right-to-left. Every rule that says 'left edge' means 'start edge', and this is the only page in the corpus that can tell the difference.
